title: Radial Derivative in Polar Coordinates
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: For z = f(x, y) with x = r cos(theta) and y = r sin(theta), find dz/dr and evaluate it at theta = 0.
finalAnswer: \frac{\partial z}{\partial r} = f_x \cos\theta + f_y \sin\theta; \quad \left.\frac{\partial z}{\partial r}\right|_{\theta=0} = f_x

steps.title: Compute Coordinate Derivatives with Respect to r
steps.explanation: Differentiate Cartesian coordinates with respect to radial distance r.

steps.title: Apply Chain Rule
steps.mathExpression: \frac{\partial z}{\partial r} = \frac{\partial z}{\partial x}\frac{\partial x}{\partial r} + \frac{\partial z}{\partial y}\frac{\partial y}{\partial r} = f_x \cos\theta + f_y \sin\theta
